items.title: Racing Santander : Yassir Zabiri dans l’équipe type de la 3e journée de Liga
items.description: Yassir Zabiri figure dans l’équipe type de la troisième journée de Liga, après sa prestation exceptionnelle avec le Racing Santander face à Elche (3-2). L’attaquant marocain a largement contribué à la première victoire de la saison du club cantabre dans l’élite espagnole en inscrivant un triplé en seulement 21 minutes. Cette performance lui permet également d’entrer dans l’histoire du Racing Santander, en rejoignant le cercle restreint des joueurs du club ayant marqué trois buts lors d’une même rencontre en Liga. Âgé de 20 ans, Zabiri a rejoint le Racing Santander le 29 juillet dernier en provenance du Stade Rennais, sous la forme d’un prêt pour la saison 2026-2027. Cette expérience en Espagne doit notamment lui permettre d’accumuler du temps de jeu et de poursuivre sa progression. Pur produit de l’Académie Mohammed VI de football, le natif de Marrakech s’était également illustré lors de la dernière Coupe du monde U20 au Chili, où il avait terminé meilleur buteur de la compétition. Après avoir débuté au KAC Marrakech, Zabiri a intégré l’Académie Mohammed VI à l’âge de 10 ans, où il a poursuivi sa formation pendant neuf années. Il a ensuite fait ses débuts professionnels avec l’Union Touarga en janvier 2024, avant de rejoindre le FC Famalicão au Portugal puis le Stade Rennais. Sa performance face à Elche et sa présence dans l’équipe type de la journée confirment ainsi le début prometteur de son aventure en Liga. The post Racing Santander : Yassir Zabiri dans l’équipe type de la 3e journée de Liga appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Trump Meant It Literally When He Said He Was Taking the Oil
items.description: “We’re going to be taking out a tremendous amount of wealth out of the ground,” Donald Trump said when he announced the capture of the Venezuelan dictator Nicolás Maduro in January. And lo and behold, it has come to pass. Trump announced last week that he had made a deal with Venezuela to develop its oil reserves. Well, not so much a “deal” as a payment by Venezuela of tribute at gunpoint. In a social-media post , Trump announced that the oil “is a Gift from Venezuela to the People of the United States.” This is a surprisingly generous offer from a country that is much poorer than the United States and, like most countries, disinclined to hand over its wealth to foreigners as a present. Venezuela’s elected representatives did not approve this deal, because Venezuela’s representatives have not in fact been elected. The country also did not hold a referendum to approve it. Instead, after capturing Maduro, whom Trump had accurately denounced as a dictator, Trump installed one of Maduro’s cronies, Delcy Rodríguez, to govern in his place, in which capacity she has displayed roughly the same level of respect for democratic norms and civil society as her predecessor. Trump’s Venezuelan-oil heist has received far less attention than either his ballyhooed promise to avoid foreign wars or his ongoing quagmire in the Persian Gulf. Yet this operation reflects Trump’s foreign-policy instincts in their most nakedly amoral—which is to say, quintessential—form. [ Gisela Salim-Peyer: The hostile corporate takeover of an entire country ] The Trump administration laid the groundwork for its intervention by painting Maduro not only as a despot but also as the leader of a criminal syndicate. The Justice Department indicted Maduro and his allies for having “acted as leaders and managers of the Cartel de Los Soles,” a derisive nickname for the country’s kleptocratic rulers. Trump, however, apparently viewed regime change as a way to exploit this arrangement rather than transform it. His invasion followed the logic not of an American president promoting democracy or regional security, but of a mobster angry to discover that a small-time crook is running a racket in his territory without giving him a taste. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, The New York Times reported in July, “has become the de facto viceroy of Venezuela, holding sway over a sovereign nation in a way that no American official has since L. Paul Bremer III arrived in Baghdad in 2003 to run U.S.-occupied Iraq.” A salient difference is that Bremer’s occupation was intended to establish the grounds for free and fair elections, which did eventually take place. Trump, in stark contrast, casually told the Times in January that he expects the United States to run Venezuela for years. The new oil deal makes that outcome more necessary and therefore more likely. Rodríguez has tied herself to a policy that is toxic to both the left and the right sides of Venezuela’s political spectrum. Left-wing Chavismos despise foreign exploitation, and the opposition resents the Chavismos’ corruption. Exposing Rodríguez’s regime to free and fair elections creates a high risk of electing a government dedicated to unwinding Trump’s deal, which gives both her and Trump a strong motive to postpone such voting. When Trump deposed Maduro, some right-of-center analysts credited him with taking the first step in what they imagined would be a democratization project. The Wall Street Journal ’s editorial board celebrated the capture as “an act of hemispheric hygiene against a dictator who spread mayhem far and wide,” as did The Washington Post ’s ( headline : “Justice in Venezuela.”) Both editorials mixed praise for the operation with caveats that the important work of transitioning to a legitimate government lay ahead, while fretting that Trump was confusing the issue with loose talk about running the country and extracting its oil. “The president often shoots from his hip in these press conferences and would be wise to reconsider,” the Post proposed. “Mr. Trump also talked about ‘the oil’ far too much,” the Journal cautioned, adding, “Sooner rather than later, Venezuela needs another election.” [ Read: The bizarre partnership between the U.S. and Venezuela ] It all sounded a bit like congratulating Michael Corleone for taking a stand against organized crime by murdering the heads of the Five Families, while urging him to clarify his intent to focus the family business on selling olive oil at market price. Venezuela’s constitution expressly prohibits the sale of its untapped oil reserves to foreign interests. But Trump’s oil deal is designed to survive democratic scrutiny. Its “structure was deliberately intended to bind future Venezuelan governments to the agreement and make it difficult to unwind,” as The Wall Street Journal characterized the explanation given by a source involved in the deal. The Journal ’s reporting suggests that Trump’s Venezuelan partners may not hold the highest regard for legal niceties. Alejandro Betancourt, the Venezuelan businessman who leads the private company partnering with the Trump administration, has been investigated for, though not charged with, money laundering. Diego Arria, a former Venezuelan ambassador now in exile in the U.S., told the Journal that the U.S. is working with Venezuelan government figures who are wanted in the U.S. for drug trafficking and other crimes. They are, in other words, Trump’s kind of partners. The president seems to despise democratically elected leaders (witness his current tantrum against Canada’s prime minister, or his yearslong feuding with South Korea, the European Union, and other erstwhile U.S. allies). He has always gotten along swimmingly with criminals (since his early days engaging in social and business dealings with mobsters in New York) and dictators (such as Vladimir Putin, whom he simply cannot quit). Trump’s favorite brand of partner combines disdain for the law and democratic norms with an absolute dependence on Trump. Trump has been saying for years that a vital objective in any foreign conflict is to seize the enemy’s oil. Indeed, he has been saying for years that he has been saying this for years. “I’ve been saying it for years. Take the oil,” he told The New York Times in 2016. Trump has shown time and again that his obsessions, even his most childish and comically sinister-sounding ones, are often quite earnest. In Venezuela, he is finally fulfilling a lifelong scheme.

items.title: Another Nollywood actor Atinuke Kareem dies after battle with cancer
items.description: Barely two weeks after the death of veteran Nollywood actor Taiwo Hassan, popularly known as Ogogo, the Yoruba film industry has suffered another loss with the death of actress Atinuke Remilekun Kareem following her battle with breast cancer. Kareem’s death was announced on Tuesday by the Ogun State chapter of the Theatre Arts and Motion Pictures Practitioners Association of Nigeria through its Executive Governor, Owolabi Ajasa. The actress had previously appealed publicly for financial assistance to enable her continue treatment for the disease. In a video released alongside the announcement, Kareem spoke about the financial strain her illness had placed on her family and appealed to members of the public to support her treatment. “I’m a breast cancer patient. It has been going on for a while. My family has spent a lot of money; I’ve come to seek help. The association I belong to, TAMPAN, has tried too, but it’s not enough,” she said. She also appealed to Nigerians to assist her, stressing that she had two young children. “Don’t allow me to die this way; I have two young children. Nigerians, please help me with any amount you can use to help,” Kareem said. Confirming her death, TAMPAN Ogun State expressed appreciation to individuals who contributed towards her treatment and offered prayers and encouragement during her illness. In a statement signed by the association’s Public Relations Officer, Femi Solaja, on behalf of Ajasa, TAMPAN acknowledged the support extended to Kareem and her family. “We sincerely appreciate everyone who contributed financially, offered prayers, encouragement, and support towards the treatment of our dear colleague, Atinuke Remilekun Kareem,” the statement said. The association described the contributions as significant to the actress and her family during her period of illness. “Your kindness and sacrifice during her difficult moment meant so much to her family and all of us. We are deeply grateful,” it added. TAMPAN said Kareem eventually succumbed to the illness despite efforts to support her treatment. “Sadly, despite all our efforts and prayers, Atinuke has passed on and answered the final call,” the statement said. The association condoled with Kareem’s family, colleagues and loved ones, while praying for strength for them to cope with the loss. “We cannot question the Almighty God. We can only submit to His will and pray that He grants her eternal rest and gives her family, colleagues, and loved ones the strength to bear this painful loss,” it added. Kareem’s death comes at a difficult time for the Yoruba movie industry, which is still mourning Ogogo, who died recently after reportedly battling stage-four cancer. The post Another Nollywood actor Atinuke Kareem dies after battle with cancer appeared first on Vanguard News .

7 suspects arrested over New Winneba attack
items.description: The Central Regional Police Command says seven suspects have been arrested in connection with the violent attack that occurred today at New Winneba in the Central Region. The incident, which is believed to have stemmed from a land dispute, resulted in the death of three people, while 19 others sustained various degrees of injury. The victims were allegedly attacked by some residents from communities within the Gomoa area. The Deputy Central Regional Public Relations Officer of the Ghana Police Service, Chief Inspector Isaac Entie, who confirmed the arrests to Adom News, said investigations are ongoing to identify other persons involved in the attack. Meanwhile, the Police Command has deployed additional personnel to New Winneba to maintain peace and order and prevent any further escalation of the situation.

items.title: Le film « 13ème Round » rafle deux nouveaux prix au Festival de Saïdia au Maroc
items.description: Le parcours international de « 13ème Round » se poursuit sous les meilleurs auspices, notamment au Maroc, où il vient de décrocher deux nouveaux prix au Festival de Saïdia. C'est ce qu'a annoncé le réalisateur Mohamed Ali Nahdi, en précisant que son long-métrage vient de décrocher le Prix d'interprétation féminine, attribué à la talentueuse actrice Afef Ben Mahmoud, ainsi que le Prix spécial du festival. En seulement deux participations au Maroc, « 13ème Round » cumule désormais trois distinctions, avec un Prix d'interprétation masculine précédemment décroché au Festival de Dakhla, sachant qu'une troisième participation à un festival au Maroc est déjà prévue au mois de novembre, précise le réalisateur. Exprimant sa profonde gratitude, Mohamed Ali Nahdi a tenu à saluer le travail de toute l'équipe artistique et technique, avant de conclure en dédiant l'ensemble de ces distinctions à « tous les anges partis beaucoup trop tôt ». Y. N. L’article Le film « 13ème Round » rafle deux nouveaux prix au Festival de Saïdia au Maroc est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: There is no missing gold – Atta Issah rejects NPP’s 16,000oz claim
items.description: Member on Parliament Finance Committee, Atta Issah, has rejected claims by the opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP) that 16,000 ounces of gold are unaccounted for in Ghana’s gold reserves. He insists there is no missing fiscal gold and argues that the discrepancy identified by the NPP is based on a flawed method of calculating the stock of gold. Speaking in an interview on Joy FM’s Top Story on Tuesday, September 1, Mr Issah said the approach used by the Minority does not take into account gold disposals and therefore cannot be relied upon to establish a shortfall. “First of all, there is no discrepancy with regards to the fiscal gold or any gold missing. There is nothing like that.” He criticised the basis of the NPP’s calculation, arguing that it is not consistent with accepted accounting principles. “How do you account for discrepancies when you haven’t taken notice of disposals? And that is not how trading account is prepared.” Mr Issah said the relevant financial statements had already provided the necessary disclosures on the gold holdings and transactions. He accused the Minority of making allegations based on assumptions rather than the contents of audited reports. “The entire press conference was purely on conjectures. It did not focus mainly on the substance.” Mr Issah urged anyone with concerns about the gold accounts to rely on the relevant sections of the auditors’ reports rather than calculations based on assumptions. He maintained that the 16,000-ounce figure cited by the NPP does not establish that any gold has gone missing, insisting that the issue should be assessed using proper accounting and disclosure standards.

Koulpélogo/Dourtenga : Les enseignants se forment au bilinguisme pour mieux accompagner les élèves
items.description: Koulpélogo/Dourtenga : Les enseignants se forment au bilinguisme pour mieux accompagner les élèves Dourtenga, 1er sept. 2026 (AIB) – Les directeurs d’écoles et les enseignants titulaires des classes de Cours préparatoire première année (CP1) de la Circonscription d’éducation de base (CEB) de Dourtenga participent, du 1er au 14 septembre 2026, à une formation sur l’enseignement bilingue, notamment en langue mooré. Dispensée par des encadreurs pédagogiques, la session vise à renforcer les compétences des participants dans l’utilisation des langues nationales comme outils d’apprentissage à l’école. Le Chef de la Circonscription d’éducation de base de Dourtenga, Yigo Diaguim, a présidé l’ouverture de la formation. Dans son discours, il a insisté sur l’importance de l’enseignement bilingue dans la vision des autorités burkinabè en matière d’éducation, notamment à travers sa généralisation progressive dans les écoles. Il a exhorté les participants à faire preuve d’assiduité, d’engagement et de disponibilité afin de tirer pleinement profit de la session et de contribuer à l’atteinte des objectifs fixés. Après son intervention, les participants ont formulé des préoccupations portant notamment sur le déroulement et les objectifs de la formation. Le CCEB leur a apporté les éclaircissements nécessaires. Les travaux se sont ensuite poursuivis avec l’intervention de l’inspecteur Issouf Kuela, l’un des formateurs. Cette première journée a notamment été consacrée à l’initiation à la transcription orthographique du mooré, considérée comme une étape dans l’acquisition des outils nécessaires à l’enseignement bilingue. À l’issue de l’exposé, les participants ont posé des questions de compréhension auxquelles le formateur a apporté des réponses et des explications complémentaires. La journée s’est achevée par des échanges sur le déroulement de la session, ainsi que sur l’organisation et le temps consacré aux différentes activités quotidiennes. Prévue jusqu’au 14 septembre, la formation se poursuivra avec d’autres modules destinés à renforcer les capacités des directeurs d’écoles et des enseignants de CP1 dans la mise en œuvre de l’enseignement bilingue. Agence d’information du Burkina AL/bp/yos

items.title: Législatives 2026 : le PAM fait du pouvoir d’achat son cheval de bataille
items.description: En présentant son programme pour les législatives de 2026, le Parti authenticité et modernité (PAM) place le pouvoir d’achat au cœur de son offre électorale. Entre réforme des circuits de distribution, baisse de la pression fiscale, soutien accru aux ménages et revalorisation des petites pensions, le parti entend répondre à une préoccupation devenue centrale. Le Parti authenticité et modernité (PAM) entend aborder les élections législatives de 2026 avec une promesse qui se veut à la fois économique, sociale et politique : rendre du souffle aux ménages. Présenté ce mardi à Rabat, le programme électoral du parti du tracteur fait du « pacte pour le pouvoir d’achat » la pierre angulaire de son projet, avec une ambition affichée de s’attaquer non seulement aux symptômes de la vie chère, mais aussi aux mécanismes qui contribuent, selon le parti, à l’alourdir. L’offensive est d’autant plus significative qu’elle intervient sur un terrain où le discours politique se heurte directement à l’expérience quotidienne des citoyens. Prix des produits alimentaires, coût de l’électricité, fiscalité sur les revenus, niveau des pensions et montant des aides sociales : le PAM a choisi de décliner sa proposition autour d’une série de mesures immédiatement lisibles, tout en cherchant à leur donner une cohérence d’ensemble. La formation politique entend ainsi faire du pouvoir d’achat non pas une promesse isolée, mais le fil conducteur d’un changement de cap. Réorganiser les circuits plutôt que simplement agir sur les prix Le premier volet du programme s’attaque à l’un des points les plus sensibles du débat sur la cherté : la formation des prix entre le producteur et le consommateur. Pour la tomate, la pomme de terre, l’oignon, la sardine ou encore les viandes rouges, le PAM met en cause les dysfonctionnements des circuits de commercialisation et le poids de la spéculation. Le parti avance notamment l’idée que les intermédiaires peuvent absorber entre 60% et 80% du prix final de certains produits. Sa réponse repose sur une réorganisation profonde des chaînes d’approvisionnement. Six sociétés régionales de distribution agricole seraient créées dans les principales zones de production, avec pour vocation d’acheter directement auprès des agriculteurs et de vendre aux détaillants. L’objectif est clair : réduire le nombre d’intermédiaires et, avec lui, la part du prix qui ne revient ni au producteur ni au consommateur. Le PAM propose également de transformer les marchés de gros en plateformes logistiques intégrées, dotées notamment de chambres froides et de dispositifs de traçabilité numérique. Dans le secteur de la pêche, des unités publiques de réfrigération seraient installées dans plusieurs ports afin de permettre aux professionnels de conserver leur production et de limiter les ventes effectuées dans l’urgence. La question agricole est, elle aussi, replacée au centre de la stratégie. Le parti souhaite conditionner certains soutiens publics à des engagements en faveur de l’approvisionnement du marché national et instaurer un contrôle préalable des exportations agricoles, avec une priorité donnée à la couverture des besoins intérieurs avant l’écoulement des excédents à l’international. Sur les viandes rouges, le programme prévoit la poursuite de la reconstitution du cheptel, la modernisation des abattoirs et un assainissement des circuits de commercialisation. Le PAM rappelle à ce propos les quelque 11 milliards de dirhams mobilisés sur 2025 et 2026 pour la reconstruction du cheptel national, dans un contexte où les mesures de soutien aux importations n’ont pas suffi à empêcher la pression sur les prix. Cette architecture traduit une conviction : la baisse durable du coût de la vie ne passerait pas uniquement par des subventions ou des mesures ponctuelles, mais par une reprise en main des mécanismes qui déterminent le prix payé par le consommateur. Du revenu disponible à la protection sociale Le « pacte pour le pouvoir d’achat » ne s’arrête toutefois pas au panier de la ménagère. Le PAM entend agir directement sur le revenu disponible des familles. La mesure la plus spectaculaire concerne la fiscalité des salaires. Le parti propose de ramener de six à trois le nombre de tranches de l’impôt sur le revenu et d’abaisser le taux marginal maximal de 37% à 20%. Les salaires bruts inférieurs à 15.000 dirhams mensuels seraient entièrement exonérés, tandis qu’un taux de 10% s’appliquerait entre 15.000 et 46.000 dirhams et un taux de 20% au-delà. Autre proposition emblématique : la gratuité des factures d’électricité inférieures à 100 dirhams pour les ménages consommant moins de 100 kWh par mois. Le dispositif serait financé par une contribution de solidarité de 12% sur la consommation dépassant 200 kWh mensuels. Le parti veut également instaurer, dès la deuxième année du prochain mandat gouvernemental, une pension minimale de 3.000 dirhams pour les retraités des secteurs public et privé dont les pensions sont inférieures à ce seuil. Il propose parallèlement de porter la pension de la veuve à l’équivalent de 100% de celle de son conjoint décédé. Le dernier étage de ce dispositif concerne les transferts sociaux. Le PAM promet de porter progressivement le montant minimal du soutien social direct de 500 à 1.000 dirhams par mois et par ménage, pour les quelque quatre millions de familles bénéficiaires. Il propose également de revoir les mécanismes de ciblage afin de limiter les erreurs d’inclusion ou d’exclusion et de les ramener à 5% à l’horizon 2030. Le parti dessine ainsi une politique de redistribution qui combine baisse de la fiscalité, réduction de certaines charges, revalorisation des revenus les plus faibles et augmentation des transferts sociaux. Une équation politique : assumer sans tout endosser C’est pourtant sur le terrain politique que le discours du PAM prend toute sa portée. Fatima Saadi, membre de la direction collective du parti, a reconnu que la formation devait assumer « sa part de responsabilité » dans la situation actuelle. Mais elle a aussitôt posé une limite : le PAM ne saurait répondre de décisions qu’il n’a pas prises ni de orientations dont il n’a pas été l’initiateur. Le message vise directement la position occupée par le parti au sein de la majorité. Le PAM rappelle qu’il est le seul partenaire de la coalition gouvernementale à ne pas avoir dirigé l’Exécutif et à ne pas avoir déterminé la politique générale du gouvernement. Certaines des propositions qu’il avait portées n’auraient, selon lui, pas bénéficié des conditions nécessaires à leur pleine mise en œuvre. Cette distinction permet au parti de tenir ensemble deux exigences contradictoires : ne pas se défausser du bilan de la majorité, tout en contestant l’idée d’une responsabilité uniforme de ses composantes. « Nous ne fuyons pas la responsabilité, mais nous ne nous attribuons pas celle des autres », a en substance défendu Fatima Saadi, appelant à ce que la reddition de comptes soit appréciée à l’aune du rôle, de la position et du poids réel de chacun dans la décision publique. Derrière cette mise au point se profile une ambition électorale plus large. Le PAM veut apparaître comme le vecteur d’un rééquilibrage, à la fois économique, territorial et générationnel. La formation promet ainsi de réduire les écarts entre catégories sociales, régions et générations, mais aussi entre ceux qui bénéficient déjà des fruits de la croissance et ceux qui attendent encore d’en percevoir les effets. Le parti place surtout la question du sentiment d’injustice au centre de son discours. « Les conflits d’intérêts ne peuvent pas continuer », affirme Fatima Saadi, qui associe cette situation au sentiment que les opportunités ne seraient pas réparties équitablement. Le choix des mots n’est pas anodin. Il ne s’agit plus seulement de promettre davantage de soutien aux ménages vulnérables. Le PAM cherche à faire de la perception de l’équité économique et de la transparence dans l’accès aux opportunités un enjeu politique à part entière. C’est dans ce même registre que la question migratoire fait irruption dans son discours électoral. Évoquant les tentatives de traversée vers la rive nord via Sebta occupée, Fatima Saadi s’est interrogée sur ce qui peut pousser de jeunes Marocains à risquer leur vie pour rejoindre l’autre rive, y compris lorsqu’ils ne sont pas issus de familles en situation de grande précarité. La question, telle qu’elle est formulée par la dirigeante du PAM, dépasse donc le seul manque de ressources. Elle renvoie à une autre dimension du pouvoir d’achat et de la politique publique : la capacité à offrir aux jeunes une perspective suffisamment crédible pour qu’ils continuent à envisager leur avenir dans leur propre pays. Le PAM entend ainsi faire de son programme davantage qu’un catalogue de mesures sociales. En plaçant le pouvoir d’achat au centre, il tente de répondre à l’une des préoccupations les plus concrètes des électeurs tout en proposant une lecture politique des déséquilibres actuels. items.title: No criminal FBI record against Tinubu – Reno Omokri
items.description: Mr Reno Omokri, Nigeria’s Ambassador-designate to Mexico, says no criminal FBI record links President Bola Tinubu to criminality. Omokri reiterated this during the City Boy Movement Podcast, anchored by Mr O’tega Ogra, on Tuesday in Abuja. He dismissed claims that FBI records relating to Tinubu established criminality, saying an FBI record should not automatically mean a criminal record. “There is no criminal FBI record against President Bola Tinubu. There’s nothing like that. “A record is just that, a record; there is a difference between a record and a criminal record,” he said. Omokri said his position was supported by an FBI record check conducted following a request by Nigerian authorities. “The result of the check was negative for any criminal arrest records, warrants or wanted status for Bola Tinubu. “So, there is no criminal FBI record against the President,” Omokri said. He said the records currently being discussed publicly by an opposition candidate originated from an earlier investigation, not a new criminal case. “There is no 2026 case. What happened is that a gentleman filed a Freedom of Information Act request. “This is not a new case; it relates to a 1993 investigation,” Omokri added. The ambassador-designate said his position on Tinubu was shaped by personal investigations and a willingness to reconsider claims when presented with verifiable evidence. He recalled travelling to the United States to investigate claims concerning Tinubu’s educational background, saying evidence obtained changed his earlier perception. “I went to Chicago State University with a witness who is still a supporter of Atiku Abubakar. “I was given incontrovertible evidence that Tinubu attended the school,” he said Omokri also said certified documents relating to Tinubu’s civil forfeiture case convinced him that some previous assertions about the President were incorrect. “I was able to get certified true copies of these documents, and they established beyond reasonable doubt that I was wrong. “This man was not who I thought he was,” Omokri said. Omokri, who previously worked politically with former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, said his support for Tinubu was based on facts and policy outcomes. “I think that I will defend the truth, whether or not I’m an ambassador or anything. “Before the President appointed me, I was defending the truth,” Omokri said. On the 2027 presidential election, Omokri said Tinubu’s economic policies substantially reflected proposals he previously advocated while working with Atiku. “If you read or listen to his speech at Chatham House, all of the things that we said we were going to do in the PDP are the things that the President is doing,” he said. He listed fuel-subsidy removal, exchange-rate reform, devolution of powers and student loans among policies he said were previously advocated. “We said we were going to remove subsidies, float the naira, devolve power from the Federal Government to states and local governments, and finally give student loans,” he said. Omokri also defended fuel-subsidy removal, arguing that restoring the policy would place unsustainable financial pressure on Nigeria. He said subsidy retention could also encourage petroleum products to flow into neighbouring countries, worsening Nigeria’s economic burden. “If you bring back fuel subsidy, you are not going to be subsidising Nigeria. You’re going to be subsidising West Africa , and that will destroy our economy,” he said. He urged Nigerians to evaluate Tinubu’s administration through measurable outcomes rather than political sentiments. “I’m not an emotional person. I’m a fact-driven person, and I believe Nigerians should also become more fact-driven,” Omokri said. He said his support for Tinubu did not mean abandoning his principles, maintaining that truth, patriotism and Nigeria’s development remained paramount. “I love this country passionately. If I die today or tomorrow, whenever I die, I want to be known as a patriot,” he said. Omokri expressed confidence that Tinubu would win the 2027 presidential election and urged Nigerians to pursue reconciliation afterwards. “The President is going to win the next election, and after that, we must all come back and reconcile. “Nigeria must continue making progress,” Omokri said. The post No criminal FBI record against Tinubu – Reno Omokri appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Koosin/Montée des couleurs : Le Haut-commissaire appelle les services de l’Etat à assurer la continuité du service public
items.description: BURKINA-KOOSIN-EDUCATION-MONTEE-COULEURS Koosin/Montée des couleurs : Le Haut-commissaire appelle les services de l’Etat à assurer la continuité du service public Nouna, 1er sept. 2026 (AIB)- Le Haut-commissaire de la province de la Koosin, Noufo Dembélé, a appelé les services de l’Etat à assurer la continuité du service public, le mardi 1er septembre 2026 à Nouna, à l’issue de la traditionnelle cérémonie de montée des couleurs qu’il a présidée en présence des forces vives de la province. Réunies autour des couleurs nationales, les autorités administratives, militaires, paramilitaires, coutumières et religieuses ont pris part à la cérémonie de montée des couleurs, marquée par l’exécution de l’hymne de la victoire, le « Ditanyè ». A l’issue de cette cérémonie à forte portée patriotique, le Haut-commissaire de la province de la Koosin, Noufo Dembélé, a livré un message aux forces vives présentes. Il est notamment revenu sur l’Immersion patriotique obligatoire (IPO), qu’il a qualifiée de réussite pour l’ensemble des acteurs ayant contribué à sa mise en œuvre. Camarade Dembélé a également rendu hommage aux Forces de défense et de sécurité (FDS) pour les sacrifices consentis dans le cadre de la sécurisation et de la libération de la province de la Koosin. Une mention spéciale a été adressée aux partenaires humanitaires pour leur accompagnement des populations. Le Haut-commissaire a, par ailleurs, déploré l’absence prolongée de certains services de l’Etat, estimant qu’elle « impacte négativement la continuité du service public ». A cet effet, il a lancé un dernier appel au service du contrôle financier, dont le fonctionnement, selon lui, ne saurait être aux antipodes de la Révolution progressiste populaire (RPP). A l’orée de la rentrée scolaire 2026-2027, l’autorité provinciale a souhaité une année scolaire apaisée et a annoncé, à ce sujet, la tenue prochaine d’une rencontre d’échanges avec les partenaires sociaux. Abordant la situation pluviométrique, Noufo Dembélé a reconnu la rareté des pluies, tout en appelant les populations à ne pas baisser la garde et à rester vigilantes, notamment en respectant les consignes de sécurité. La prochaine cérémonie de montée des couleurs est prévue en octobre 2026 au service du contrôle financier. Agence d’information du Burkina AC/HB/OO

items.title: Houet : Un enfant talibé grièvement blessé hors de danger, la responsable interpellée
items.description: Houet : Un enfant talibé grièvement blessé hors de danger, la responsable interpellée Bobo-Dioulasso, 1er septembre 2026 (AIB) – Un enfant talibé, âgé de 13 ans, grièvement blessé dans la nuit du dimanche à Bobo-Dioulasso, par une dame a été admis le lundi nuit au Centre hospitalier universitaire (CHU) de Pala. Il est aujourd’hui hors de danger, a appris l’AIB. La dame, elle, a été interpellée. Selon le procureur du Faso près le Tribunal de grande instance de Bobo-Dioulasso, Sékou Traoré, joint par l’AIB, l’enfant talibé, âgé de 13 ans, aurait été grièvement blessé dans la nuit du dimanche 30 août 2026 à Bobo-Dioulasso, par une dame qui l’aurait accusé de vol. La dame aurait porté des coups de couteau, occasionnant des entailles aux membres supérieurs et à la tête du talibé, a précisé le procureur, s’appuyant sur les premiers éléments d’information recueillis par ses services. Une source témoin de la scène et jointe par l’AIB a indiqué avoir conduit la victime d’abord au CMA de Dafra, qui l’a ensuite référée au CHU de Pala au regard de l’étendue des blessures. Le service de communication du Centre hospitalier universitaire (CHU) de Pala joint au téléphone par l’AIB a confirmé l’admission de l’enfant lundi nuit au sein de la formation sanitaire et indique qu’il est hors de danger. Saisi ce mardi matin de la situation et au regard de la gravité supposée des faits, le procureur du Faso a indiqué à l’AIB, avoir instruit les services compétents de dresser la procédure et de procéder à l’arrestation de la mise en cause, en vue de son déferrement, « en attendant une meilleure appréciation des faits que l’enquête révélera » a-t-il ajouté. Agence d’information du Burkina AB/wis

items.title: Karo-Peli/Arbinda : Sport, cohésion et fraternité au terme du « Tournoi de l’Espoir »
items.description: BURKINA-MARACANA-AGENTS-SECURITE-ARBINDA Karo-Peli/Arbinda : Sport, cohésion et fraternité au terme du « Tournoi de l’Espoir » Arbinda, 29 août 2026 (AIB) – La première édition du tournoi de maracana dénommé « Tournoi de l’Espoir » s’est achevée samedi à Arbinda dans une ambiance festive, avec la victoire de l’équipe A du 28ᵉ Bataillon d’intervention rapide (BIR) face à celle des Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie (VDP), sur le score d’un but à zéro. L’événement a mobilisé les Forces de défense et de sécurité (FDS), les VDP, les autorités locales et les populations autour des valeurs de cohésion et de fraternité. La journée de clôture a débuté par un grand cross populaire à travers les principales artères de la ville. FDS, VDP, autorités administratives locales, services techniques et populations de différentes couches sociales ont pris part à cette activité, témoignant d’une forte mobilisation autour de cette initiative sportive. Les activités se sont poursuivies dans l’après-midi sur le terrain départemental devant une importante mobilisation populaire. Un match de gala féminin a ouvert les festivités sportives, avant la finale de pétanque qui a vu l’équipe de la mairie s’imposer face à l’équipe 3 des VDP. Le point d’orgue de la journée a été la finale du tournoi de maracana. Au terme d’une rencontre disputée et engagée, l’équipe A du 28ᵉ BIR a pris le dessus sur celle des VDP sur le score d’un but à zéro. La cérémonie de clôture s’est déroulée en présence du Camarade Président de la Délégation spéciale de la commune d’Arbinda, Lazard KIEME, entouré des membres de la délégation spéciale, des responsables des services techniques ainsi que du représentant du Commandant du 28ᵉ BIR, parrain de la cérémonie. À travers cette première édition, le « Tournoi de l’Espoir » a permis de rapprocher les différentes composantes de la population et de promouvoir les valeurs de solidarité et d’unité au sein de la commune d’Arbinda. Agence d'information du Burkina. MW/zs

items.title: Guerra híbrida contra Europa
items.description: “No estamos en guerra, pero tampoco ya en paz”, advierte desde hace meses Friedrich Merz. Podría parecer una afirmación exagerada o alarmista. No lo es. El Gobierno alemán acusó este martes a Moscú de estar detrás del ataque con drones en el aeropuerto de Leipzig el 4 de agosto pasado, y certificó así el diagnóstico del canciller, que vale tanto para Alemania como para el conjunto de Europa. Las campañas de desinformación, intimidación, sabotajes en territorio europeo empezaron hace años y no son ninguna novedad, pero desde la invasión rusa de Ucrania hace cuatro años no han dejado de intensificarse y en los meses recientes han adquirido una nueva dimensión. No son escenarios hipotéticos sin impacto en la vida real ni tampoco un conflicto remoto y abstracto. Cuando una potencia nuclear como es Rusia intenta un atentado en el corazón de Alemania, como denuncia Berlín, ya no puede hablarse de simples injerencias, sino de actos de guerra híbrida, o de guerra a secas. items.title: UK-based Nigerian falls asleep at wheel after almost 3 days of driving, kills man
items.description: A Nigerian-British taxi driver, Kolawole Erunkulu has been jailed for six years after falling asleep at the wheel and causing a crash that killed a 59-year-old man in Surrey, UK. Surrey Police said Erunkulu of Bexleyheath, pleaded guilty to causing death by dangerous driving after his Audi crossed into a roadside layby and struck Philip Dray. The fatal collision happened shortly before 6.30am on Sunday, August 17, 2025, on the A23 in Merstham. Philip had safely parked his Volkswagen in a layby to take a break and was opening the driver’s door to get back into his vehicle when he was hit by Erunkulu’s Audi. He died at the scene. CCTV footage showed the Audi’s nearside wheels crossing completely over the white lines into the layby before correcting course following the collision. Detectives investigating the crash examined footage from Erunkulu’s vehicle and data obtained from his employers. The investigation found that he had driven for about 53 hours during the three days before the collision. Police said his longest rest period during that time was only seven hours, while other breaks included one of approximately four hours and two of around two hours. In the 12 hours immediately before the crash, Erunkulu had been working as a taxi driver with only short breaks. Footage from an interior camera in his vehicle showed Erunkulu experiencing what police described as a “microsleep” — a brief episode of sleep lasting only seconds. During one of these episodes, the vehicle veered across the carriageway and struck Philip, who was standing in the layby. The footage showed Erunkulu continuing to drive for about another 10 seconds before stopping at the next layby. Erunkulu, who holds joint British and Nigerian nationality, was charged with causing death by dangerous driving in March 2026. He pleaded guilty when he appeared in court in June. At Guildford Crown Court on Tuesday, August 25, he was sentenced to six years in prison. Police said he would have received a nine-year sentence had he been convicted following a trial. He was also disqualified from driving for eight years, running concurrently with his prison sentence, and will be required to pass an extended driving test if he applies for a new licence. During sentencing, Judge Lees said the footage showed Erunkulu was “extremely tired” but continued driving despite his condition. “The footage shows the defendant was extremely tired and, in my view, has continued to drive when he must have known that,” the judge said. She added: “All of this could have been stopped had he have slept.” Acting Detective Inspector Rob Baldwin, of Surrey Police’s Serious Collision Investigation Unit, said the case highlighted the dangers of driving while fatigued. “Mr Erunkulu had worked long hours with insufficient rest over the preceding days, accumulating a sleep debt,” Baldwin said. He warned that fatigue could severely affect a driver’s ability to remain alert and react safely, particularly during the early hours of the morning when the natural drive to sleep is strongest. “Anyone who feels tired should not continue driving, as the consequences can be devastating,” he said. Philip’s family described him as an “amazing partner and man”, saying he was dependable, caring and someone others could rely on. His sister said Philip was a careful and conscientious driver who spent his life prioritising the safety of his passengers and other road users. His partner described him as a “sweet, gentle, and caring man” and said they had been each other’s “cheerleader, advisor, partner, and best friend”. She said Philip was her “partner and soulmate” and that his death had left an “enormous emotional and physical void”. The family has agreed to the release of footage showing Erunkulu falling asleep at the wheel in an effort to highlight the dangers of driving while fatigued. Afghan-origin doctor, policeman among eight held; meth worth Rs900m seized
items.description: KARACHI: A police task force on narcotics in Karachi, in collaboration with a federal civilian intelligence agency, carried out an intelligence-based raid on a warehouse in Mehran Town, Korangi, on Tuesday, arresting eight members of an alleged “international narcotics network” and recovering 50kg of crystal meth, also known as ice, worth Rs900 million. Speaking at a press conference, West Deputy Inspector General of Police Irfan Ali Baloch said the suspects were allegedly operating an international narcotics network and transporting drugs from Pakistan to Thailand and Malaysia in bulk quantities. He said the police had recovered 50kg of ice, estimated to be worth Rs900 million. He revealed that the consignment intercepted before export weighed between 200kg and 250kg and had an estimated value of $25 million to $30m (Rs6 billion to Rs8bn). He added that more consignments were expected to arrive in Karachi from Balochistan. “Acting on credible information, the task force, in conjunction with the intelligence agency, established that the narcotics were being concealed in crates of tiles and marble at a warehouse in Mehran Town for export to the Philippines under the cover of a ‘legitimate’ consignment,” DIG Baloch said. “A covert operation was mounted against an international network trafficking methamphetamine (ice) to Malaysia and the Philippines.” Sharing details of the trafficking routes and the network’s linkages, DIG Baloch said the present consignment was destined for the Philippines from Karachi, with overseas handlers in South Africa and Thailand. He said the network had established links in Karachi, while the ice was sourced from Chaman in Balochistan and hawala transactions were routed through Lahore. Regarding the roles of the eight suspects, DIG Baloch said Nazir Soomro was the principal accused who directed the procurement, concealment and export of the consignment. He added that Shahid Mastoi arranged and maintained the Mehran Town warehouse used to conceal the narcotics, while Sheikh Khalid provided storage for the drugs and facilitated banking channels for local transactions. According to the DIG, Dr Noor Ahmed Khilji and Garan Khan, both of Afghan origin and holders of Pakistani CNICs, arranged the supply from Balochistan. Abdullah alias Wahab worked as a courier, while Mohammed Kamran, also a courier, was a police constable posted in Malir. Nasir worked as an intermediary and distributor, facilitating transactions involving Dr Noor. He said the police recovered 50kg of ice, along with a car, two pistols and Rs350,000, from the suspects. The DIG said the ice was procured locally at Rs220,000 per kilogram and contracted for export at $6,000 per kilogram, against an estimated destination-market price of $100,000 to $120,000 per kilogram. Of the 200kg to 250kg contracted for export, the remaining quantity had not been delivered, he said, adding that the full consignment had an estimated destination-market value of $25 million to $30m (Rs6bn to Rs8bn). Organised network DIG Baloch said the case pointed to an “organised network” with domestic and international linkages involving procurement, financing, concealment and attempted export. He said the concealment of the narcotics in a commercial consignment of marble indicated the “deliberate exploitation of legitimate trade channels”. “Overseas handlers, suppliers, financial facilitators, warehouse operators and clearing agents indicate a structured supply chain, not an isolated attempt,” the senior officer said. He feared that had the consignment reached its destination, it could have caused reputational damage to Pakistan internationally. Tracing foreign linkages DIG Baloch said the narcotics task force, which also included the Special Investigation Unit (SIU), was further questioning the arrested suspects to establish the full network, identify additional facilitators and beneficiaries, and trace the complete financial trail, including the cryptocurrency advance and local accounts used in the transactions. He added that the task force was also verifying the identities and roles of foreign handlers in Malaysia, Thailand and South Africa in coordination with other law-enforcement agencies, customs authorities and international counterparts to trace the network’s overseas linkages.

items.title: Nervios y miedo entre familias migrantes acampadas en las calles de Ceuta: “Damos vueltas para encontrar dónde dormir”
items.description: “Ojalá no nos lo hubieran dicho”. El martes a las siete de la mañana, un grupo de mujeres migrantes se presentó en una de las naves del Polígono de El Tarajal de Ceuta en las que trabajaban agentes de Policía Nacional a decirles que un empleado de seguridad les había avisado de que el jueves a mediodía ya no podían seguir acampados en sus calles. Les dijeron que se calmaran y se sentaran, pero aseguran que no les dieron ninguna explicación. Cuando vieron que no las atendían, empezaron a dar vueltas por la ciudad autónoma, para ver dónde podrían instalarse. Farah Dayay y Nihad, dos mujeres marroquíes emigrantes de 40 y 26 años con niños de 14 y cuatro años a su cargo, estaban entre ellas. “Hemos estado dando vueltas para encontrar dónde dormir, hemos preguntado en el Príncipe, en Sidi Embarek [donde los vecinos tienen campamentos para mujeres y niños] pero nada, tenemos miedo de lo que vaya a pasar con nosotros”, decía Dayay. Fuentes del Gobierno aseguran a EL PAÍS que no consta ningún operativo de desalojo previsto en esta zona para ese día. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Déraillement de RUSAL à Dubréka : Fassou Théa tape du poing sur la table face au péril écologique
items.description: Le ministre de l’Environnement et du Développement durable, Fassou Théa, s'est rendu en urgence à Kagbelen Village ce 1er septembre 2026, dans la préfecture de Dubréka. Ce déplacement officiel visait à évaluer sur le terrain l'ampleur des dégâts environnementaux et les risques sanitaires consécutifs au déraillement d'un train minéralier transportant de l'alumine, opéré par la société RUSAL. Accompagné d’une délégation de cadres techniques et d'experts de son département, le Chef du ministère ne s'est pas limité au simple constat des dégâts matériels sur les infrastructures ferroviaires. L'inspection a permis de cartographier plusieurs foyers de déversement accidentel d'alumine à ciel ouvert, à proximité immédiate des habitations du village. Bien que les équipes du ministère assurent une veille environnementale depuis l'accident survenu dans la soirée du samedi 22 août dernier, Fassou Théa a vivement regretté le manque de communication de la multinationale, qui n'a envoyé aucune notification officielle aux autorités de tutelle après le sinistre. Face à la presse, le ministre a rappelé les priorités de son action : « En pareille circonstance, il y a la sécurité et la santé des populations. Mais également, en cas de déversement, nous devons essayer de voir les produits chimiques qui sont déversés, procéder à leur analyse et examiner leur impact sur la santé publique ainsi que sur l’écosystème. C’est ce qui explique notre présence ici ce matin. » En l'absence de confinement des matières déversées, le ruissellement des eaux de pluie risque d’entraîner l'alumine vers les cours d'eau adjacents et d'altérer durablement les nappes phréatiques locales. Le ministre a fermement enjoint la direction de RUSAL à déployer un plan d'action de sécurisation immédiat. « Donc, nous avons conseillé à notre partenaire Rusal de prendre toutes les dispositions nécessaires afin que ce déversement ne puisse pas impacter non seulement la santé des populations riveraines, mais également que cela ne soit pas une source de lessivage en cas de pluie, susceptible d’impacter les cours d’eau à proximité ». Au-delà de la pollution physique, c'est l'organisation interne de la compagnie minière qui a suscité l'indignation de la délégation officielle. Aucun représentant du département Santé, Sécurité et Environnement (SSE) de RUSAL n’était présent pour accueillir l’inspection ministérielle. « Notre premier constat n’est pas satisfaisant, car nous n’avons trouvé aucun responsable environnement de la société sur place. Nous avons rappelé à l'entreprise que cela devait être une priorité absolue », a martelé Fassou Théa, rappelant les obligations réglementaires des industriels en République de Guinée. Une réunion de crise programmée dans les prochains jours au siège du ministère devra dresser un bilan technique approfondi de la situation et acter des mesures de suivi et de réparation environnementale strictes.

items.title: 2027: Turaki-led PDP endorses G100’s move to challenge Tinubu
items.description: The Tanimu Turaki-led faction of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has endorsed the G-100, a group of 100 opposition stalwarts driving the creation of an all-opposition front to challenge President Bola Tinubu of the APC in the 2027 presidential election. The faction, in a statement by the National Publicity Secretary of the PDP Interim National Working Committee, Mr Ini Ememobong, on Tuesday in Abuja, said the decision to join forces with other credible political forces was informed by the challenges Nigerians face under the ruling party. “Our participation is anchored on the premise that the process will be hinged on the philosophical underpinnings of transparency, equality, data-driven decisions and egalitarianism. “Any result birthed by a process midwifed by these virtues will certainly offer Nigerians a credible leadership capable of alleviating the skyrocketing poverty and rising insecurity in the country,” it said. The party stated that the new move aligned with its earlier stated disposition of working with like-minded political parties and organisations desirous of ‘rescuing’ Nigeria. “Our participation at the first meeting of the G-100 on 31st August, 2026 is a further indication of our preparedness to contribute our quota in the quest for an all-opposition platform that will take power from the incumbent and rebuild Nigeria for the good of all Nigerians,” it said. The post 2027: Turaki-led PDP endorses G100’s move to challenge Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Three dead, 15 injured in violent clashes at New Winneba
items.description: Three people have been confirmed dead and about 15 others injured following violent clashes at New Winneba in the Central Region on Tuesday, September 1. The Ghana Police Service said one of those injured is a police officer, with all the injured persons receiving treatment at the Trauma and Specialist Hospital in Winneba. According to the Police, the violence began at about 10:40 a.m. when about 300 people armed with guns, stones, cutlasses and sticks allegedly stormed New Winneba Township. Read also: IGP deploys reinforcement team to contain violence in New Winneba shooting incident The group, reportedly from Gomoa Oguakrom, Gomoa Yenkuadze and Gomoa Pomadze, allegedly attacked residents and vandalised shops, stores and other properties belonging to people in the community. Personnel from the Winneba Divisional Headquarters and Agona Swedru District Patrols were subsequently deployed to contain the violence and restore calm. The Inspector-General of Police, Christian Tetteh Yohuno, has also ordered additional security personnel from the National Police Headquarters to reinforce the operation. The reinforcement includes two armoured vehicles deployed to support efforts to prevent further escalation. The Police Service says the situation is currently under control, with security personnel remaining in the area to maintain peace and prevent further disturbances. The cause of the clashes and the circumstances surrounding the deaths are still being investigated. The Police said further details would be provided as investigations continue.

items.title: Conakry: une unité de fabrication de yaourt clandestine démantelée avec une importante production
items.description: Les Services Spéciaux ont découvert, ce mardi 1 er septembre 2026, un lieu clandestin de fabrication de produits laitiers dans la capitale. L’opération a permis de saisir 1 410 boîtes de yaourt et 794 boîtes de Hamza dans le quartier Hamdallaye, destinées à la distribution dans des boutiques de Conakry. Sur place, les agents ont constaté des conditions d’hygiène jugées non-conformes. Des seaux éparpillés dans la pièce, des emballages posés à même le sol et les conditions de conservation ne respectaient pas les normes. « Nous avons trouvé des personnes qui manipulent des produits laitiers dans des conditions impropres », a déclaré le commissaire principal de Police, Soropogui Foromo, de la direction chargée de la lutte contre le crime organisé. Selon lui, l'enquête a été menée à partir d'opérations de filature auprès de distributeurs afin d'identifier les lieux de fabrication. « Le lait est un milieu de culture bactérienne très puissant. Cela peut évidemment entraîner la maladie au niveau des consommateurs », a-t-il averti. Cinq personnes ont été interpellées et conduites auprès des officiers de police judiciaire pour les besoins de l’enquête. Les activités ont été arrêtées et le local fermé. Présent lors de l’opération, Boubacar Guissé, Inspecteur général adjoint du Contrôle de qualité, a relevé plusieurs irrégularités. « Le fabricant de lait n'a pas l'autorisation de fabriquer ce genre de lait. L'endroit n'est pas approprié, il n'a pas ses certificats d'analyse », a-t-il expliqué. Il rappelle que la loi alimentaire prévoit, pour ce type d’infraction, un à trois ans de prison ferme et une amende de 10 à 50 millions de francs guinéens, en plus des poursuites judiciaires. Les autorités invitent enfin les citoyens à signaler les lieux où des produits alimentaires sont fabriqués ou conservés dans de mauvaises conditions. « N'importe qui peut tomber sur ça : mes enfants, les enfants d'autrui, les parents », a souligné Boubacar Guissé.

items.title: PM Shehbaz says water ‘lifeblood’ of region, must never be weaponised
items.description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday said water was the “lifeblood” of the region and must never be weaponised, as he addressed a summit of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) in Kyrgyzstan. Speaking at the SCO Council of Heads of States (CHS) meeting in the Kyrgyz capital Bishkek, the premier said the region cannot “realise its full potential without lasting peace”. Without naming India directly, he highlighted the issue of the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) and demanded that it be honoured. “Water is the lifeblood of our region. It sustains millions of lives, nourishes our land and secures the very future of our coming generations,” he noted. He stressed that it “must never be weaponised; it cannot be used as an instrument of coercion, nor can it ever be exploited for political leverage”. “The treaties governing our shared waters are solemn, binding international commitments. They are not matters of political convenience to be cast aside at your will. They must be honoured unconditionally, in both letter and spirit.” In a later statement on X, the premier said he was honoured to address the ceremony as Pakistan assumed chairmanship of the SCO, reiterating that water “is the lifeblood of our region” and must never be weaponised by any state. He also noted that Pakistan made “immense sacrifices in the fight against terrorism”, and added that Pakistan will conduct its chairmanship of the body under the theme ‘Turning Vision into Action: Connectivity, Innovation and Shared Prosperity’. “I am confident that the SCO will continue to grow from strength to strength and bring meaningful improvements to the lives of its more than 3 billion people,” he writes. The prime minister’s speech comes a day after the Permanent Court of Arbitration (PCA) ordered India to uphold the IWT with Pakistan and suspend work on a hydro project in occupied Kashmir. The Hague-based court backed Pakistan’s stance, declaring that the IWT between the two countries remained fully in force, as India had no justification for ending or suspending the agreement. Water and the IWT remain a contentious issue between India and Pakistan, following New Delhi’s unilateral abeyance of the accord in April last year — a move that was followed by a brief military conflict between the two sides in May 2025. ‘Terrorism one of the gravest threats’ Speaking on the issue of terrorism, PM Shehbaz said it remained “one of the gravest threats that has affected our entire region in its various forms and manifestations”. As chair of the SCO Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS), Pakistan has “worked actively to strengthen regional counter-terrorism cooperation”, he highlighted. “Few nations have fought against the scourge of terrorism as resolutely and valiantly as Pakistan. In the past two and a half decades, we have sacrificed more than 90,000 lives and endured economic losses of over $150 billion in combatting terrorism.” Pakistan sought a peaceful and stable Afghanistan, he said, adding: “But let there be no ambiguity; so long as terrorists continue to use Afghan territory to shed the blood of innocent Pakistanis and other nations, lasting peace will remain beyond our reach.” In his speech, the prime minister also mentioned Pakistan’s mediation efforts in the US-Iran war and laid out the country’s plan as it assumed the SCO CHS chair. PM Shehbaz was welcomed by the Kyrgyz president upon his arrival at the summit’s venue on Tuesday, and later posed with other world leaders for a group photo. Leaders from China, Iran, Turkiye, Russia, and India were also in Kyrgyzstan for the two-day summit. The regional bloc, which also includes Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan and Belarus, is celebrating its 25th anniversary. A video clip shared by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) showed PM Shehbaz speaking to China’s President Xi Jinping. He could also be seen sitting together with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan. The premier also held informal meetings with the presidents of Iran, Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan and Belarus. Taking SCO chair, Pakistan proposes ‘excellent plan’ Pakistan has assumed the chairmanship of the SCO CHS for 2026–27, with next year’s summit to be hosted by Islamabad. “As Pakistan assumes the chairmanship of the SCO, we are proposing an excellent plan that will prioritise key sectors, including IT and AI, energy development, poverty reduction, disaster management, health, culture and sports,” PM Shehbaz said during his address. As part of that plan, Pakistan proposed establishing an SCO framework for sovereign AI infrastructure and governance to “promote responsible and inclusive AI development and to also ensure that no member state is left behind”. The prime minister said Pakistan’s SCO chairmanship will be pursued under the theme, ‘Turning vision into action, connectivity, innovation and shared prosperity’. “We undertake this responsibility with humility, hope and abiding faith that connectivity will bring our peoples closer, innovation will open new doors of opportunity, and shared prosperity will reach every home,” the premier said. He called for turning the SCO vision into action and its promises into progress. PM Shehbaz said: “Let us […] move forward together with the resolve that, in a time of uncertainty, history will record the SCO as having chosen cooperation over confrontation, dialogue over division, and hope over fear. “Let history record that the SCO did not merely witness a changing world; we shaped it together.” The premier noted that the SCO region was inhabited by over 3bn people and blessed with abundant natural resources. “This extraordinary potential also places upon us SCO leaders an extraordinary responsibility to shape a better future for our peoples.” He recalled that he has long advocated for regional connectivity as the “key to our prosperity”. “Today, connectivity is no longer a choice; it is a strategic imperative. The regional crisis has also proven that diversified transport networks, secure energy corridors and resilient supply chains are indispensable to our collective security.” PM Shehbaz said the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) continued to “serve as a gateway, linking the regional economies to the Arabian Sea”. He affirmed that Islamabad remained committed to advancing existing trans-regional railway projects, road connectivity initiatives and regional energy projects. The prime minister called for ensuring the implementation of the SCO Development Strategy until 2035, adding that the establishment of the SCO Development Bank would be a “critical step” in this regard. As the permanent chair of the Special Working Group of the SCO on Poverty Reduction, Pakistan will continue to strengthen social protection and promote inclusive and sustainable development across the SCO region, he pledged. ‘Intensifying geopolitical tensions’ The premier noted that today’s global landscape “is marked by intensifying geopolitical tensions, fragmenting global economy, escalating climate crises and unprecedented technological transformation”. “In such a complex environment, the SCO represents our collective resolve to navigate through these enormous challenges together and deliver peace, security and prosperity to our peoples,” he observed. The prime minister affirmed that Pakistan “consistently upholds and respects the core principles of both the UN and SCO charters”. “We remain committed to resolving disputes peacefully through international law, adhering strictly to the guidelines of the SCO charter.” He highlighted that in line with this spirit, Islamabad “staunchly advocated peace when the sovereignty and territorial integrity of an SCO member state was violated earlier this year, triggering a major regional crisis”. PM Shehbaz then noted that Pakistan and the international community have “borne a heavy economic cost ” as the “closure of critical energy supply routes” disrupted the global economy, referring to the Strait of Hormuz . “In these challenging times, Pakistan has consistently acted as an honest and sincere mediator and facilitator,” he affirmed. He recalled that Islamabad’s “sustained diplomatic efforts culminated in the signing of the landmark Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding” in June, terming the document a “critical step towards regional de-escalation and the restoration of peace”. The premier noted that peace-building efforts were continuing and extended his “deepest gratitude to the brotherly and friendly countries, many of whom are represented here today, for their unwavering support throughout this endeavour”. “We firmly believe that the Islamabad MoU offers the most viable and enduring pathway to lasting peace in the region.” The 14-point MoU , signed in June, provided a framework for ending the war that began with US-Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28. It was a result of mediation efforts spearheaded by Pakistan and others. Besides signing the Islamabad MoU as the mediator, Pakistan had also brokered a ceasefire between the US and Iran in April. The April ceasefire put an end to the most intense fighting, but sporadic attacks, mainly around the Strait of Hormuz, have dimmed the prospects of a final peace agreement. At the SCO summit, the prime minister also mentioned the signing of the trilateral defence pact between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye last month, named the “ Makkah Defence Alliance ”. He reiterated that the pact was “fundamentally defensive in nature and is neither directed against any state nor intended to create any confrontation or division whatsoever”. He emphasised that while Pakistan has always strived to strengthen multilateralism, “multilateral organisations must be empowered to translate aspirations into action”. “The plight of the innocent people of Gaza and West Bank continues unabated, causing unimaginable suffering. Palestinian mothers endure the profound grief of mourning their children, families remain torn apart, and entire generations continue to live under a perpetual shadow of fear, deprivation and gross injustice.” The premier called upon the international community to honour its commitment to “help the Palestinian people, alongside all other oppressed nations, secure their fundamental right to self-determination”. On Monday, Israeli airstrikes killed five people around Gaza City, a local hospital and rescuers said. Despite a US-backed ceasefire that took effect in October 2025, violence has not halted in the Gaza Strip, with Israel continuing to target Palestinians it claims are fighters. At the outset of his speech, PM Shehbaz congratulated the Kyrgyz Republic on the completion of its “successful SCO chairmanship and for making impressive contributions to further advance practical cooperation among the SCO members”. The prime minister also felicitated the leadership and people of Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan for their respective independence days. The premier described the gathering as “historic” and extended his gratitude to Kyrgyz President Sadyr Nurgozhoevich Japarov and his team for their hospitality and “excellent arrangements” made for the summit. “Guided by the Shanghai spirit, Pakistan takes great pride in being part of the SCO, as we celebrate 25 years of this remarkable journey, a milestone for which I congratulate all fellow members,” PM Shehbaz told the summit. “From a tender sapling, the SCO has grown into a towering tree, providing the shade of security and stability for all of us.” Lahore named SCO’s Tourism and Culture Capital for 2026-27 The city of Lahore has been named the Tourism and Cultural Capital for 2026-27 by the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO). The title of Tourism and Cultural Capital has been rotated annually among SCO member states since 2022, and the designation serves to highlight the prominence of a city that embodies the cultural heritage of the country that takes over the rotating presidency of the organisation. The designation is designed to promote people-to-people contacts and tourism among the member states. Cities that have held the title in the past include Varanasi, India (2022-23), Almaty, Kazakhstan (2023-24), Qingdao, China (2024-25) and Cholpon-Ata, Kyrgyzstan (2025-26). The decision to designate Lahore as the tourism and cultural capital was taken in April this year, when the heads of tourism administrations of SCO member states met in Bishkek. UN urgently in need of reform, PM tells SCO Plus summit PM Shehbaz also addressed the SCO Plus summit, an expanded format of the regional bloc. The prime minister noted that the United Nations was established to “fulfil the universal dream of ending all wars and building enduring peace”. Stressing that Pakistan has remained fully committed to the UN Charter in the past eight decades, he said: “We see the rise of a multipolar world as an opportunity to build a more equitable, democratic and just international system. “But today, the UN is urgently in need of reform. It must become more accountable and responsive.” As a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council , Pakistan has been “actively contributing to global peacemaking over the past two years”, PM Shehbaz highlighted. He noted that these efforts culminated in the signing of the Islamabad MoU, stressing that it offers a “widely accepted basis for all parties to pursue peace through dialogue and diplomacy”. Speaking about the Makkah defence pact, PM Shehbaz said the agreement “has further strengthened the prospect for peace in the region by sending a message of unity and common resolve, as well as to promote progress and prosperity in the region”. He reiterated his concerns over the situation in Gaza and the occupied West Bank, terming it “deeply troubling”. The premier demanded that the international community “act decisively and now to end the suffering of innocent Palestinian people and uphold their inalienable right to self-determination”. “The same rights must also be granted to all other oppressed nations around the globe.” The premier reiterated his remarks about the water issue in his address to the SCO Plus Summit. Speaking on terrorism, he affirmed Pakistan’s commitment to battling the “three evils of terrorism: separatism, terrorism and religious extremism” under the SCO’s RATS. “We believe that terrorism, in all its forms and manifestations, including state terrorism, must be condemned in clear and unambiguous terms,” he asserted. The prime minister stressed the need for the SCO to “deliver tangible dividends to its peoples”. “I reaffirm Pakistan’s solemn resolve and commitment to realise the true potential of the SCO. In our efforts to elevate the SCO to even greater heights, we seek the kind cooperation of SCO member states, as well as our valued SCO Plus family.” He then invited the participants to the next edition of the SCO Plus summit set to be held in Islamabad. View this post on Instagram The government later said that PM Shehbaz met UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres on the sidelines of the summit. PM pledges to boost cooperation with Belarus On the sidelines of the summit, PM Shehbaz met Belarusian President Aleksandr Lukashenko, and both leaders expressed satisfaction with the positive trajectory of bilateral ties and cooperation across the political, trade, and economic spheres, among others. In a statement posted on X, the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said that both leaders pledged to boost cooperation in trade, industry, agriculture, IT and vocational training as priority sectors, with PM Shehbaz extending an invitation to Lukashenko to once again visit Pakistan. Lukashenko visited Pakistan in 2024, with PM Shehbaz visiting Belarus last year. “Both leaders reaffirmed their shared commitment and resolve to elevate the long-standing friendly relations between Pakistan and Belarus to new heights,” the statement read. Lahore named SCO’s Tourism and Culture Capital for 2026-27 The city of Lahore has been named the Tourism and Cultural Capital for 2026-27 by the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO). The title of Tourism and Cultural Capital has been rotated annually among SCO member states since 2022, and the designation serves to highlight the prominence of a city that embodies the cultural heritage of the country that takes over the rotating presidency of the organisation. The designation is designed to promote people-to-people contacts and tourism among the member states. Cities that have held the title in the past include Varanasi, India (2022-23), Almaty, Kazakhstan (2023-24), Qingdao, China (2024-25) and Cholpon-Ata, Kyrgyzstan (2025-26). The decision to designate Lahore as the tourism and cultural capital was taken in April this year, when the heads of tourism administrations of SCO member states met in Bishkek. Dar meets counterparts from Iran, China, others On the sidelines of the twin SCO summits, DPM Dar interacted with the foreign ministers of China, Russia, Iran, Uzbekistan , Azerbaijan , Tajikistan , Belarus and Armenia , among other leaders. The Foreign Office (FO) shared pictures of Dar, Iranian FM Abbas Araghchi, Russian FM Sergey Lavrov, Tajik FM Sirojiddin Muhriddin and Kazakh FM Yermek Kosherbayev having a “warm and cordial interaction”. Earlier in the day, Dar, who arrived in Bishkek a day ago to join PM Shehbaz, had a “warm exchange” with Iran’s Araghchi. Dar stressed that the “sincere implementation” of the Islamabad MoU was the only way forward amid the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, according to FO. Describing the meeting as a “warm exchange”, FO said the two ministers exchanged views on bilateral relations and regional developments and reaffirmed the importance of continued engagement. “The DPM underscored that dialogue and diplomacy remain essential to promoting peace and stability in the region, and that sincere implementation by both parties to the conflict of the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding of June 2026 remains the only way forward,” FO said in a statement on X. A day ago, PM Shehbaz had met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on the sidelines of the summit in Bishkek and underscored the need to build on the understandings reached under the Islamabad MoU. Dar “held a warm and cordial exchange” with China’s FM Wang Yi, FO said. Both leaders reaffirmed the All-Weather Strategic Cooperative Partnership between Pakistan and China. They also discussed matters of mutual interest, including the upcoming United Nations General Assembly session this month in New York and the ongoing process for the election of the next UN secretary-general. DPM Dar also met with the director of Türkiye’s National Intelligence Organisation (MİT), İbrahim Kalın. “The two sides exchanged views on regional developments and matters of mutual interest, including the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement and the inaugural meeting of its Strategic Political and Defence Committee, as well as recent developments in the region,” FO said. Dar underscored the importance of continued coordination and diplomatic engagement for regional peace, security and stability. The deputy premier and his Russian counterpart Alexei Overchuk had a “productive exchange of views on bilateral relations”, FO said. They reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening the close Pakistan–Russia partnership, enhancing cooperation, and maintaining high-level engagement between the two sides. They also discussed regional and international developments of mutual interest.

items.title: Le projet « daara-atelier » veut enrôler près de 600 talibés par an
items.description: En visite de courtoisie, lundi 31 août, auprès de Serigne Cheikh Mouhamadou Mahi Ibrahima Niass, khalife général de Médina Baye, le ministre de l’Emploi et de la Formation professionnelle et technique a insisté sur l’intérêt que l’État accorde à la mise en œuvre du projet « daara-atelier ». Celui-ci, a déclaré Idrissa Samb, ambitionne de former près de 600 talibés par an dans les cités religieuses. KAOLACK- À la tête d’une forte délégation, comprenant notamment le préfet de Kaolack et des responsables de son département, le ministre de l’Emploi et de la Formation professionnelle et technique a effectué, le lundi 31 août 2026, une visite de courtoisie auprès du khalife général de Médina Baye, Cheikh Mouhamadou Mahi Ibrahima Niass. Devant le guide religieux, Idrissa Samb est largement revenu sur le projet « daara-atelier », un concept novateur initié par l’État du Sénégal en 2025. « Nous sommes dans le mois de Gamou qui célèbre la naissance du Prophète (Psl). Mais nous en avons aussi profité pour présenter au khalife le projet « daara-atelier », une initiative que l’État a mis à la disposition des foyers religieux. Son objectif est de permettre aux apprenants (talibés) de s’initier à certains métiers. La finalité est que ces derniers soient opérationnels une fois leur formation terminée », a expliqué le ministre. À Médina Baye, dit-il, le projet s’articule autour de quatre composantes. Il s’agit de la filière froid et climatisation, la structure métallique, l’aviculture et l’agroalimentaire. Des métiers porteurs qui, selon le ministre de l’Emploi et de la Formation professionnelle et technique, ont été choisis par le khalife général lui-même. « À Médina Baye, nous avons pour ambition de former près de 600 talibés par an dans ces métiers », a indiqué Idrissa Samb, rappelant que l’objectif global de l’État étant de former grâce à ce projet, au moins 15.000 talibés d’ici à 2029. À Kaolack, pour mettre en œuvre celui-ci, Cheikh Mouhamadou Mahi Ibrahima Niass a mis à la disposition du ministère une assiette foncière destinée à accueillir certaines infrastructures. « Nous tenons à remercier le khalife qui a mis à notre disposition un hectare et demi de terre pour y installer le projet », a indiqué le ministre. Selon M. Samb, le lancement du marché interviendra sous peu afin de permettre le démarrage effectif des travaux. À travers cette initiative, le ministère, a-t-il affirmé, entend faire de la formation professionnelle et technique un véritable levier d’autonomisation, d’inclusion et d’insertion socioéconomique des talibés. Une démarche saluée par le khalife général de Médina Baye, qui a exprimé sa satisfaction et son soutien à cette initiative visant à offrir aux pensionnaires des « daara (écoles coraniques) » des compétences et de nouvelles perspectives d’avenir. Il en a profité pour formuler des prières à l’endroit du Chef de l’État et de son gouvernement. « Je remercie le ministre et sa délégation pour le déplacement. Nous prions pour la paix à travers le monde, car sans elle, nous ne pouvons rien accomplir. Le développement de ce pays doit être au centre de nos préoccupations. Je prie pour le président de la République et l’ensemble de son gouvernement. Nous sommes un seul peuple et il doit en être ainsi pour toujours », a déclaré Cheikh Mouhamadou Mahi Ibrahima Niass. Avant Médina Baye, le ministre de l’Emploi et de la Formation professionnelle et technique s’était rendu la semaine dernière à Tivaouane et à Ndiassane, des foyers religieux concernés également par le projet. « Nous allons étendre le projet sur le territoire national et dans tous les foyers religieux », a affirmé Idrissa Samb.
